reply:
HttpOnly doesn't protect localStorage. HttpOnly is a cookie flag. It prevents script from reading cookies. localStorage has no such protection—any script can read it directly.

If the JWT is in localStorage (as you said), an XSS script exfiltrates it without touching cookies or HttpOnly at all. It just calls `localStorage.getItem('token')`.

Cost of this setup: XSS is common (dependencies, typos in templates, DOM APIs). Token in localStorage + XSS = attacker has a valid JWT they can use server-side, on any device, for as long as it's valid. That's account takeover.

HttpOnly cookies would close this. They trade CSRF risk (mitigated with SameSite), but they stop the localStorage path entirely.

grade.note: Correctly reiterates that HttpOnly only protects cookies, not localStorage, with clear mechanism explanation.
